clear_size_metric.compatibility: a record of a legacy version (1 or 2) that carries neither the per-episode field nor the summary section still verifies; a version 3 or 4 record must carry it, so deleting it from a current record is reported instead of verifying. A present section is compared with the same type-and-key rules as the mandatory ones, and in a legacy record presence is all-or-nothing across the complete suite — every episode and every agent summary in one record — so a record that stripped the histogram from one agent while another kept it, or that reports totals its episodes do not carry, is rejected rather than verified with a partial histogram. Records written by the pre-change writer for experiments 000, 001 and 002 verify end to end (see legacy_experiment_records).

objective_record.compatibility: a legacy suite record (version 2) without the section still verifies, which is what keeps the runs of this experiment written before it existed valid; a version 4 Tetris suite must carry it, so deleting the section from a newly written record is reported — before this repair it verified with `verify_run` returning [], which is the reviewer's counterexample. A record whose configuration has no Tetris agent must not carry it, because no writer emits one.
objective_record.place: a top-level suite section beside the frozen heuristic mapping, never a leaf inside an episode or its result; required by a version 4 suite that uses the Tetris agent, optional only at the legacy version 2
objective_record.source: tetris.weights_record(): the declared weights, the well-depth cap and the tie-break rule
objective_record.verification: verify_run compares the recorded module name and weights with the current module's under the same exact type-and-key rules it applies to the heuristic mapping, so a suite that uses the Tetris agent cannot verify under a different objective merely because the change preserved its replayed choices; live play, the second path that writes suite records, records the same section for a live Tetris game; the current versions require the section, because absence alone cannot tell a legacy record from a current one whose section was deleted
objective_record.why: the frozen heuristic mapping is recorded for every suite because every placement agent scores through it, and the Tetris agent's choices come from a second, separately declared objective; before this section existed a suite record was tied to its objective only through the replayed choices, so a changed objective still verified whenever the change happened to preserve them

publication.compared_paths: every path either tree tracks, plus this worktree's untracked files, derived from Git: a declared list can omit a path the task changes, and the review found that hole twice (first this record's own result.json, then any tracked path outside the list); 46 paths in the published tree at this round's run
publication.note: publication is service-owned and gated on an exact-tree approval, so the branch ref and the PR head move together: the probe asserts that the two refs name one commit and that the commit descends from the recorded base, and it compares the repaired paths' content — per-file sha256 in the published clone beside this worktree's — instead of their presence, which cannot tell a published repair from an earlier publication that contains the same file names. When the contents differ it requires the difference to be exactly the repair this worktree holds uncommitted, prints the differing paths and reports the earlier-publication state instead of calling the repair published; a published tree differing from a clean worktree fails
